'''Alan Mark Portis''' (July 17, 1926 &ndash; September 6, 2010<ref name="sciencetoday">[http://scitation.aip.org/content/aip/magazine/physicstoday/news/10.1063/PT.4.1925 Death notice. Alan M. Portis], ''[[Physics Today]]'', March 4, 2011. [[American Institute of Physics]].</ref>) was an American [[solid-state physics|solid-state]] [[physicist]] and founder of the Berkeley Physics Laboratory.

==Career==
Alan Portis was the dean of engineering at Berkeley as well as an engineering professor.<ref name=TST/> He was an early researcher in [[electron paramagnetic resonance]].<ref>{{Cite book|url = https://books.google.com/books?id=1LdKSYIQtPYC|title = Foundations of Modern EPR|last1 = Eaton|first1 = Gareth R.|last2 = Eaton|first2 = Sandra S.|date = 1998-01-01|publisher = World Scientific|isbn = 9789810232955|language = en}}</ref> He also founded the Berkeley Physics Laboratory.<ref>{{Cite book|url = https://books.google.com/books?id=280NAQAAIAAJ|title = Mechanics|last1 = Kittel|first1 = Charles|last2 = Knight|first2 = Walter D.|last3 = Ruderman|first3 = Malvin A.|last4 = Helmholz|first4 = A. Carl|last5 = Moyer|first5 = Burton J.|date = 1973-01-01|publisher = McGraw-Hill|isbn = 9780070048805|language = en}}</ref><ref>"Use of the Berkeley Physics Laboratory to Teach an Advanced Physics Course". ''[[The Physics Teacher]]''. James David Logan. Mar 73. Vol. 11 issue 3. pp. 147–149.</ref> For the development of laboratory courses and curricula at [[UC Berkeley]], he received the [[Robert A. Millikan|Millikan Medal]] from the [[American Association of Physics Teachers]].<ref name=TST>"Scientists Decry a Slick New Packaging of Creationism". William J. Bennnetta. ''[[The Science Teacher]]''. May 1987.  pp. 36–43 (43).</ref>  Portis was the doctoral advisor of the 2000 [[Nobel Prize|Nobel Prize laureate in Chemistry]] [[Alan J. Heeger]],<ref>[http://www.physics.berkeley.edu/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=42&Itemid=294 Nobel laureates], Department of Physics, [[University of California, Berkeley]].</ref> as well as [[Nai Phuan Ong]] and Myron Salamon, both of whom were elected Fellows of the American Physical Society.

Portis was a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim Fellow]] in 1965.<ref>[https://www.science.org/doi/abs/10.1126/science.209.4459.895 AAAS Annual Elections], ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'', 22 August 1980: Vol. 209 no. 4459, pp. 895–915</ref>
Portis was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in February 1976.<ref>[https://www.science.org/doi/abs/10.1126/science.192.4236.277 AAAS Council Meeting, 1976 .] ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'', 16 April 1976: Vol. 192 no. 4236, pp. 277–281.</ref> He was also a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name="sciencetoday"/>

Portis was also the first director of Berkeley's [[Lawrence Hall of Science]], and one of the founders of the Search for Excellence in Science and Mathematics (SESAME) Group at UC Berkeley.{{citation needed|date=November 2013}}
